actions_or_findings.title: CURRENT_TASK_BLOCKER: Wrong OTP attempts roll back
actions_or_findings.trigger: Either phone-change OTP is wrong or expired.
actions_or_findings.rationale: _apply_otp updates attempt or expiry state, then _raise_otp throws inside run_owned_transaction. The rollback discards that state. The change endpoint has no separate attempt limit, so a valid-session holder can repeatedly guess a phone OTP without exhausting its configured attempts. The unit tests mock away the transaction.

actions_or_findings.title: CURRENT_TASK_BLOCKER: Concurrent refresh can survive session revocation
actions_or_findings.trigger: An old-session refresh commits while phone change scans active sessions.
actions_or_findings.rationale: Refresh locks its session and creates a successor, while phone change scans sessions with an unlocked SELECT. If the scan occurs before refresh commits, phone change can revoke the old row yet miss the new successor. This violates the requirement to revoke all old sessions. The successful run checked only sequential access and refresh.

actions_or_findings.title: NON_BLOCKING: The old masked number remains the default account label
actions_or_findings.trigger: A user created by SMS login changes phone without editing their display name.
actions_or_findings.rationale: Initial registration sets display_name to the old masked phone; phone change leaves it in place. Both inspected screenshots still show that label after success and new-phone login. The database evidence supports that the credential changed, but the label is misleading.
